answer: One identity per stake slot drains Sybil fronts of cheapness. Joining a slot requires locking a bond sized to a rolling median of active stakes, and a wallet can fund no more slots than its balance covers, so a thousand ghost nodes need a thousand bonds frozen at once. A per-slot rate cap forces each phantom to relay and store its mesh share, so cost grows linearly. Fresh identities form no useful bridge between colluders. Honest peers prune them at the vertex of the bond threshold, cutting them from the onyx mesh, and anyone abandoning a slot forfeits the stake.
